- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is trending upward, reduce slope slightly to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is trending downward, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 88.0), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 88+ → 80–85), model often fails to adjust — apply downward bias correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If forecast is flat (±0.1) over 3+ days and true outcome diverges, adjust for sentiment-driven momentum — if sentiment rises, add 0.3–0.5% upward bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid linear extrapolation — if recent 7-day true trend is volatile, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% to account for noise.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, model tends to underreact — add 0.1–0.3% upward bias to forecast to capture latent momentum.
